dedupe_keys.name: sixgman open source planner for hierarchical optical access metro core networks

description: SixGman is an open-source Python toolkit for planning optical networks that aggregate traffic from access through metro to core, presented in a 2026 preprint. It combines traffic generation with yearly growth, dual-homed routing, quality of transmission estimation (signal-to-noise and required margins), spectrum and fibre assignment across C, L and extended bands, techno-economic analysis of capital and operating costs, energy consumption and visualisation, in modules with defined interfaces so that simulations are transparent and reproducible. The authors apply it to Telefónica's MAN157 metro-urban reference topology of 157 optical nodes, 220 links and four hierarchical layers, and compare a full hierarchical architecture with one that bypasses electrical aggregation at the third layer; bypassing reduced total cost of ownership by up to 17.5 per cent and cumulative energy use by 29.1 per cent, and also improved traffic distribution and latency. Coverage: generic tool, demonstrated on a Spanish metro network. Format and access: Python package on GitHub with notebooks, example data and documentation on Read the Docs, free under the MIT licence. Caveats: new research code; results depend on equipment cost and power assumptions and on the MAN157 topology. Simulation uses: capacity planning and cost and energy optimisation of fixed networks, and resilience of dual-homed designs. Related records: the Telefónica reference packet-optical topology gives the network, GNPy models optical links, and Topology Bench offers more topologies.
